positive.note: The configured bind is a literal loopback address and the child's bound listener re-checks loopback before serving.

native.path: Start -> normalizeUI -> ui.ValidateBind -> MayListen refuses 0.0.0.0, ::, 192.168.1.10, fe80::1 and a hostname before the instance root exists; Start -> startUI -> uiChild.supervise -> launch (re-exec --fae-internal-ui) -> ui.Main -> ui.Run -> MayListen accepts the bound 127.0.0.1 listener

limits: The post-bind re-check in ui.Run is reached natively only on the accept path; its refusal needs a non-loopback bound address, which ValidateBind already refuses. Requirement mapping is limited to the named predicate and cited tests; no complete requirement acceptance is claimed.

positive.note: A loopback peer addressing the listener's own host with the token (header, cookie or one-time query exchange) is served.

native.path: Start -> startUI -> uiChild.supervise -> launch -> ui.Main -> ui.Run -> server.ServeHTTP -> MayServeRequest: an anonymous /healthz is refused 401, a token-bearing /api/status is served

limits: The foreign-Host and non-loopback-peer refusals are unit-only (ui package).

positive.note: With the daemon-issued write capability the one UI write (alert acknowledgement) goes through the daemon RPC with an authorizing message.

native.path: Start (UI AllowWrites) -> uiChild.supervise -> launch -> ui.Run -> server.ServeHTTP -> acknowledge -> MayWrite -> AlertAcknowledge RPC, audited as ui-writer; an undirected message is refused by the daemon

limits: Native evidence is accept-path; the read-only refusal (no write capability) is shown by the ui package test. The first argument is always true at the call site: request authentication is MayServeRequest's job.

positive.note: A killed UI child is restarted within the per-window bound while the drive completes a task.

native.path: Start -> startUI -> uiChild.supervise -> MayRestartUIChild: one restart after SIGKILL is admitted; a child that always dies is left stopped after the lowered bound of 3 with exactly one ui-child alert

limits: The tests lower the Appendix A bound (10 per hour) through fastUISupervision; the stopping branch is exercised by shutdown, not asserted separately.

positive.note: Under the -1 defaults two revisions run concurrently; tasks of an already running molecule are never capped.

native.path: Start -> drive -> dispatchTask -> releasesMolecule -> CanReleaseIntoMolecule: with an instance limit of 1 (and with max_running 1 declared in content) the second revision's molecule is withheld as molecule_limit until the first ends

limits: The per-workflow limit is reached natively through content (max_running); the instance-wide limit through Config.MaxMolecules.

positive.note: Frozen RED evidence always suffices; a no-red task whose diff the target classifier calls non-code lands.

native.path: Start -> drive -> liveExecutor VcsCommit -> commitPolicy -> CanCommitWithoutRed: a no-red task with production code in its diff, and a no-red task without a declared classifier, escalate NoRedViolation before any commit object; a classified non-code diff lands

limits: The RED-preferred branch (hasRed) is reached natively by every RED task; the ROB-013 resume case (declared no-red with valid frozen RED) is unit-only.

positive.note: QA proved the exact committed tree under the pinned target's always-required tests and compile check, so the commit proceeds.

native.path: Start -> drive -> liveExecutor VcsCommit -> commitPolicy -> CanCommitTree: a tree proved by QA (requiredProofKey marker) commits across a restart; a workflow that never runs the required tests escalates RequiredCheckFailed with no commit

positive.note: A local effect interrupted after its completed daemon receipt is adopted at recovery without re-running or charging the task.

native.path: SIGKILLed helper daemon, then Start -> loadJob -> recoverInFlight -> adoptCompletedEffect -> CanAutoAdoptEffect: completed, host-completed and integrate-completed receipts are adopted; completed-tampered (postcondition mismatch) and prepared stay parked UncertainDispatch

limits: The first two arguments are always true at the call site (the receipt lookup and lease retirement return earlier on failure), and the external case returns before the guard; those refusals are shown by the truth table and the formal mutation, not by a daemon test.
